fields.meta_title: Crypto Landing Page Builder for Web3 Products | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a crypto landing page from one prompt. Examples include a wallet beta waitlist and a bug report form for a protocol. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Crypto Landing Page for Your Wallet or Protocol
fields.hero_description: Build a crypto landing page for a wallet or a protocol, with forms that save each signup to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: The Forms and Alerts Behind a Crypto Page
fields.features_subheading: A crypto landing page explains one product and asks for one action. Emergent builds the page with its form and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your description

Describe the product, who it is for, and the one thing a visitor should do. Emergent builds the page and the form under it from that prompt, and a second prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_2:
Signups in a database you own

Each form entry is saved as a row in a database you own, and every answer, such as a phone type or a wallet address, gets its own column. Filter it to see who joined after a post.
fields.feature_3:
Alerts for the entries that need a person

Name in the prompt which entries need a human, such as a large store or a Critical bug. The app sends that person an email, Slack, or in-app alert carrying the details of the entry.
fields.feature_4:
Connected to the tools you already run

The app connects to any tool with an API. Signups can flow to the CRM or email tool the team uses, and bug reports reach the support desk without anyone copying them by hand.
fields.feature_5:
The project's own name in the address bar

Put the page on a custom domain such as brisawallet.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. A visitor checking the address before signing up sees the real name.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, ready for review

The free tier covers building and publishing the page. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, where any developer can review and extend it.

fields.tab_content_1:
One beta waitlist, sorted by phone into two invite lists

Brisa Wallet opened its beta with a waitlist that asks for an email and a phone type. The app saves that choice on each row, then emails the iOS list when the iOS beta opens and the Android list when that build is ready. Of 2,860 signups, 1,710 chose iOS and 1,150 chose Android.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every hackathon team registers with a public repo link

Teams register for the Quarry Labs hackathon with a team name, a public repo link, and a track. The form asks again when the link is not a full https:// address, before the team is saved. Of the 186 teams that signed up, 74 picked Tooling, 63 Gaming, and 49 Payments.
fields.tab_content_3:
Dalia Restrepo gets every store over 500 orders a month

The demo form for Saffron Rail, a checkout plugin that lets online stores accept crypto, asks for the store platform and the orders a month. A store over 500 orders a month emails sales lead Dalia Restrepo with its details, and the rest join the demo queue. In October, 41 of 312 requests went to Dalia and 271 to the queue.
fields.tab_content_4:
When a report is Critical, Joon-ho Baek gets the email

Security reports for Basalt Protocol arrive through a form that asks for the affected contract, a severity, and the steps to reproduce. Each Critical report emails security lead Joon-ho Baek with the contract name and the steps. The first month brought 58 reports: 3 Critical, 11 High, and 44 Medium or Low.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Crypto Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan and test a crypto landing page with one clear action and a form that saves every entry.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Say what it does in one line
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Check each field before a row is saved
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide the one step a visitor takes, such as joining the beta or requesting a demo. Put that form near the top of the page, where it shows without scrolling, and move the roadmap and team bios below it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the headline as a plain statement of what the product does and who it is for, such as a self-custody wallet that keeps the keys on the phone. Save the protocol detail and the jargon for the docs.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the sections and form fields, then the rule for each entry: who gets an alert, and which entries wait in a queue. Emergent builds the page with a database behind it, and you change either one by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Have the form check each field's format before it saves anything. A repo link should be a full https:// address, and a wallet address should be the right length for the chain the product runs on. A typo then gets fixed by the visitor, not by you.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Label every field in plain words
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write each label the way a visitor would say it, such as Wallet address or Phone type, and add one line under any field that needs a reason. Mark which fields are optional, and keep the required ones to what the next step needs.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Show who is behind the project
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name the team or the company, link the public code, and say where security reports go. If an outside firm reviewed the contracts, link its full report from the page instead of quoting a summary of it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on a phone, then share the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on your own phone twice, once with clean entries and once with a broken link, then check the table and the alerts. After that, give each channel where you announce the page its own link.

faq_plan.q: What is a crypto landing page?
faq_plan.a: A crypto landing page is a single web page for one crypto product, such as a wallet, an exchange feature, or a protocol. It explains what the product does and asks the visitor to take one step, such as joining a waitlist or requesting a demo. It describes the product, not the price of a token.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a crypto landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product and the one form you need in a prompt, and Emergent's AI landing page builder builds the page with a table for every entry. Say who should get an alert, such as a sales lead for large stores, and change the page later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What sections does a crypto landing page need?
faq_plan.a: It needs five parts: a headline that says what the product does, a short section on how it works, the one form, a section that names the team and links the public code, and a short FAQ. Add a page for security reports if the product holds user funds. Emergent writes each section from a plain-English prompt, and you change any of them by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: Can one crypto landing page cover a wallet and a token launch?
faq_plan.a: It can, but give each its own page so each keeps a single action: the wallet page collects beta signups, and the launch page collects its own list. A collectible drop is a third case and gets its own nft landing page, built around the artwork and an allowlist.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect wallet addresses on a crypto landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a wallet address field to the form and check its format before the row is saved. The ethereum.org docs say an externally owned account has a 42-character address. A shorter paste can then go back to the visitor for a fix. Ask only for a public address, never a seed phrase or a private key.

faq_plan.q: What claims should a crypto landing page leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out price and return talk: no price predictions, and no promise that a token will be worth more. Keep the page to what the product does today, what a visitor gets by signing up, and who runs the project.

faq_plan.q: How do I run a beta waitlist on a crypto landing page?
faq_plan.a: Ask for an email and the one detail that decides who gets in first, such as phone type or country, and save each signup as a row. Email each group when its build is ready. To reward early signups with a prize draw, run that on a separate giveaway landing page with its own rules. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Does a crypto landing page need a connect wallet button?
faq_plan.a: No, only when the visitor has to sign or send something on the page itself. A waitlist or a demo request needs only an email and a few fields. When a page does need the button, EIP-1193 is the standard to read: it formalizes an Ethereum Provider API to promote wallet interoperability.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a headline for a crypto landing page?
faq_plan.a: Name the product and its job in under 10 words, such as Open-source tools for testing smart contracts. Put the supported chains or the one key detail in the line under it. When two headlines both read well, Emergent can build a second version of the page from one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which channel brought crypto landing page signups?
faq_plan.a: Give each channel its own link with UTM tags, and save the tags with each signup. The Google Analytics help page lists utm_medium as the marketing medium, for example cpc, banner, or email. A paid post on LinkedIn can point to a linkedin landing page written for that audience.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this keyword is design galleries, stock vectors and template files (Figma, Envato, Dribbble, a Webflow cloneable, an ICO template roundup, a GitHub concept repo): they show how a crypto page looks and stop before a visitor does anything on it. This page shows four crypto product pages built from a prompt and follows what happens after the visit: a wallet beta waitlist split by phone type, a hackathon registration that checks each team's repo link, demo requests for a checkout plugin where large stores reach the sales lead by email, and a protocol's bug report form where a critical report emails the security lead. Builder intent only: no price, token value, return or investment talk anywhere, and the how-to and FAQ say to leave it out. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, sections, one page per product, wallet addresses, claims to leave out, a beta waitlist, the connect-wallet button, the headline and tracking signups by channel.

Quarry Labs registers hackathon teams with a team name, a GitHub repo link and a track, the form sends back any link that does not start with https://github.com/, and 186 teams signed up: 74 Tooling, 63 Gaming and 49 Payments.

Saffron Rail's demo request form for its checkout plugin asks for the store platform and monthly orders, and each request over 500 orders a month emails sales lead Dalia Restrepo: 41 of 312 requests in October.

Basalt Protocol's bug report form asks for the affected contract, a severity and the steps to reproduce, and each Critical report emails security lead Joon-ho Baek: 58 reports in the first month, 3 Critical, 11 High and 44 Medium or Low.
